name: Metricool
tagline: Schedule posts and consolidate basic account analytics for a few profiles
verdictSummary: The core loop is buildable, but a dependable replacement becomes a real weekend or multi-day project. For Metricool, schedule posts and consolidate basic account analytics for a few profiles. The hard boundary is many social apis, reporting, ad integrations, inbox, and creator workflow, plus api access, connector upkeep, and collaboration.
coreLoopDIY: Draft and schedule posts for a few profiles, preview them accurately, publish through one official API, consolidate basic account analytics, and retain a searchable content calendar.
requirements: developer application for one social network
whatYouLose: many social APIs, reporting, ad integrations, inbox, and creator workflow
moatNotes: API access, connector upkeep, and collaboration
ongoingBurden: OAuth review, API policy changes, media limits, queues, retries, rate limits, webhooks, tokens, and moderation workflows
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Metricool because the scheduler is easy; staying approved and correct across constantly changing social APIs is the subscription. The recurring cost buys OAuth review, API policy changes, media limits, queues, retries, rate limits, webhooks, tokens, and moderation workflows, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Postiz
priorArt.desc: Active open-source social media scheduling platform.

alternatives.name: BrightBean Studio
alternatives.desc: Publishing plus cross-account analytics, with an inbox for good measure; public competitor research is not included.

facts.install: Hosted signup, or clone the repository and deploy with Docker Compose or a supported PaaS.
facts.engines: No model is bundled; its REST API and MCP server connect external agents such as Claude Desktop/Code, Cursor or custom clients.
facts.dataFormat: Hosted data lives in BrightBean's cloud; self-hosted data uses PostgreSQL 16+ with media on local disk or S3-compatible storage.
facts.gapVsPaid: BrightBean does not match Metricool's mature competitor tracking, advertising analytics and client-ready reporting.
facts.setupBlocker: Connecting social networks requires first-party platform developer/OAuth credentials; self-hosting also requires Docker or a PaaS.

alternatives.name: Buffer Free
alternatives.desc: Three profiles, ten queued posts each and basic analytics; eight lifetime channel connections is the hidden ceiling.

facts.install: Hosted signup, with optional desktop browser extension and mobile apps.
facts.engines: Buffer AI Assistant is included, but Buffer's public product documentation does not identify its underlying model provider.
facts.dataFormat: Posts, media, ideas, connected-account metadata and analytics are stored in Buffer's cloud.
facts.gapVsPaid: Buffer's free analytics are lightweight and omit Metricool's competitor, ad and consolidated reporting depth.

alternatives.name: Mixpost Lite
alternatives.desc: Single-user scheduling with basic account analytics and queues; the free edition stays deliberately small.

facts.install: Docker Compose is recommended; a manual Laravel/Composer installation is also documented.
facts.dataFormat: MySQL stores application data, Redis handles queues/cache, and media uses local/public disk or S3-compatible storage.
facts.gapVsPaid: Mixpost Lite supplies only basic account analytics, not Metricool's cross-network reporting and competitor analysis.
facts.setupBlocker: Requires a server with Docker plus social-platform app credentials; the manual path also needs PHP, Composer, Supervisor, cron, Redis and FFmpeg.

alternatives.name: Postiz
alternatives.desc: Multi-network scheduling and account analytics; self-hosting replaces the bill with infrastructure.

facts.install: Hosted signup, or Docker Compose for self-hosting.
facts.engines: Optional AI/media features connect to OpenAI, ElevenLabs, fal.ai, Tavily, KieAI and Transloadit.
facts.dataFormat: PostgreSQL holds application data; Redis and Temporal support jobs; media is stored locally or in Cloudflare R2/S3-compatible storage.
facts.gapVsPaid: Postiz's analytics are less mature than Metricool's and come with a substantial self-hosted operations burden.
facts.setupBlocker: Hosted use is straightforward; self-hosting requires Docker, social OAuth apps, and a PostgreSQL, Redis and Temporal stack.

alternatives.name: Social Champ Free
alternatives.desc: Three non-X accounts with scheduling, analytics and an inbox; the missing X connection is not subtle.

facts.install: Hosted signup and OAuth connection to each social profile.
facts.engines: Champ AI Suite is included, but Social Champ's public documentation does not identify the underlying model provider.
facts.dataFormat: Posts, media, profile metadata, inbox data and analytics live in Social Champ's cloud.
facts.gapVsPaid: Social Champ Free excludes X and offers much shallower reporting than Metricool's paid analytics workspace.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Metricool Free
rejectedAlternatives.desc: It omits LinkedIn and X and stops at twenty posts a month; that is below Metricool's actual job.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Starter plan and a single-network scheduler DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a personal replacement for Metricool in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, Drizzle ORM, and one official social-platform API; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: draft and schedule posts for a few profiles, preview them accurately, publish through one official API, consolidate basic account analytics, and retain a searchable content calendar.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Support drafts, scheduled times, queues, campaigns, tags, and a weekly calendar.
Connect exactly one social network using its documented OAuth flow.
Validate character, media, aspect-ratio, and file-size limits before scheduling.
Publish through an idempotent background job with retries and clear failure states.
Store platform post identifiers and refresh publication status without scraping.
Add reusable snippets, local media storage, CSV export, and a token reconnect flow.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Deliberately leave out unofficial automation or scraping.
Deliberately leave out multi-network inbox and social listening.
Deliberately leave out agency approvals, white labelling, and enterprise reporting.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
